full_judgment:
KM Hafizul Alam J: This Rule, at the instance of the petitioner, was issued under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1898 (in short, the Code) calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Special Case No. 24 of 2015 arising out of Palong Police Station Case No. 4 dated 17-8-2004 corresponding to GR No. 480 of 2004 under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 now pending before the learned Special Judge, Faridpur should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule, is that on 17-8-2004 one Md Shahidul Islam, Assistant Inspector, District Anit-Corruption Bureau, Shariatpur as informant lodged a First Information Report (hereinafter referred to as FIR) with Palong Police Station being Palong Police Station Case No. 04 dated 17-8-2004 under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the accused-petitioner No. 1. The allegations were that the accused-petitioner No. 1 was appointed as Commander of Muktijoddha Sangsad, Shariatpur District Unit vide appointment letter dated 11-12-1996 issued by the signature of the then Chairman of Muktijoddha Sangsad Abdul Ahad Chowdhury. Thereafter the accused-petitioner No. 1 received pay order No. 520413 dated 12-4-1998 for an amount of Taka 3,00,000 and pay order No. 0016748 dated 19-4-1998 for an amount of Taka 8,84,500 from the Central Command Council of Muktijoddha Sangsad for getting lease of Dubisayor Haat or Kazir Haat. The accused-petitioner No. 1 submitted the said pay orders infavour of the Deputy Commissioner, Shariatpur and got lease of Dubisayor Hat for the Bengali year 1405. The accused-petitioner No. 1 was supposed to return the said money to the Central Command Council of the Muktijoddha Sangsad by collecting the same from the Haat. But the accused-petitioner No.1 never returned the said money. Thereafter, the accused-petitioner was removed from the post of District Unit Commander on 16-7-2001 for misappropriation of Taka 11,84,500. The accused-petitioner No. 1 was also during the period of 11-3-1999 to 8-5-2001 vide 62 (sixty two) bank cheques withdrew Taka 12,37,500 from the account of Shariatpur District Unit of Muktijoddha Sangsad maintained with Agrani Bank, Shariatpur Branch without any approval of the District Unit Command: Lae also could not show any account of the said money for which the same has been spent. The petitioner No. 1 in the year 1998 without any resolution or approval also sold out the tinshed old office of the Shariatpur District Unit Commands at the price of Taka 25,000 whereas the market price of the said tinshed house Was at Taka 50,000. Thus the accused-petitioner Not .1 in total misappropriated Taka 24,47,000. The accused-petitioner No.1 also without handing over the relevant documents/account destroyed the records in order to avoid the punishment for misappropriation of above mentioned money and thereby he committed offence under section 201 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 3. Thereafter, one Md Shahidul Islam Deputy Assistant Director of the Anti-Corruption Commission (in brief the ACC), Integrated District Office, Faridpur as Investigating Officer after investigation submitted 4 (four) separate charge-sheets. Charge-sheet No. 24 dated 28-2-2012 has been submitted against the petitioner No. 1 under sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 and charge-sheet Nos. 24/1, 24/2 and 24/3 all dated 28-2-2012 have been submitted against the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 4. Subsequently the case was transferred to the court of learned Special Judge, Faridpur for trial and the same was re-numbered as Special Case No. 24.2015. After that the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application for discharging them under section 265C of the Code before the learned Special Judge Court, Faridpur. But the learned Judge vide order dated 1-2-2016 rejected the said application of the petitioners. Subsequently the learned Judge framed charge against the petitioners under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 on 9-5-2016. 

 6. At the time of Rule hearing, Mr Sifat Mahmud, learned advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (in brief the ACC Act, 2004) was promulgated on 23-2-2004 and the said Act, 2004 came into force on 9-5-2004 repealing the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957. But sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 were not in the schedule of the ACC Act, 2004. 

 7. Mr Mahmud next submits that inspite of the clear previsions of law the Assistant Inspector of the then Bureau of Anti-Corruption as informant lodged the instant FIR on 17-8-2004 against the petitioner No. 1 under sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 after 3(three) months of the said Act, 2004 which is illegal and without any lawful authority as such the proceedings of the instant case under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 is not a proceeding in the eye of law and the same is liable to be quashed. 

 8. Mr Mahmud further submits that the Deputy Assistant Director of ACC was assigned to investigate the instant case under sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 on 8-2-2011 but at the relevant time of approval of the ACC for investigation of the case, the above mentioned sections were not in the schedule of the ACC Act, 2004. Therefore, the charge-sheets dated 28-2-2012 against the petitioners under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 are without lawful authority as such the instant proceeding is not a proceeding in the eye of law and the same is liable to be quashed. 

 9. Mr Mahmud lastly submits that section 420 of the Penal Code, 1860 was included in the schedule of the ACC Act, 2004 on 20-11-2013 but the investigation Officer got approval for investigation on 7-2-2011 and he submitted charge-sheets on 28-2-2012 against the petitioners under sections 406/420/201/ 109 of the Penal Code, 1860 hence the ACC did not have any authority to investigate the instant case as such trial of the instant case on the basis of charge-sheets dated 28-2-2012 cannot be proceeded against the petitioners, therefore, the proceeding of the instant case is liable to be quashed. 

 12. Mr Rouf further submits that though section 420 of the Penal Code, 1860 was not included at the time of lodging FIR in the schedule of the ACC Act, 2004 but it was in the schedule of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957. 

 18. On perusal of the records, it appears that pursuant to the DABER No. 02/2002, the preliminary inquiry was started against the petitioner No. 1 for alleged offence committed during the period of April 1998 to May 2001. But before lodging the FIR, the ACC Act, 2004 was passed by the parliament on 23-2-2004 and this Act has come into force with effect from 9-5-2004. Thereafter, the FIR was lodged by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption on 17-8-2004 under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860. Subsequently one officer of the ACC investigated the case and submitted 4 (four) separate charge-sheets. Charge-sheet No. 24 dated 28-2-2012 has been submitted against the petitioner No. 1 under sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 and charge-sheet Nos. 24/1, 24/2 and 24/3 all dated 28-2-2012 have been submitted against the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860. Thereafter, the learned Special Judge, Faridpur framed charge against the petitioners under sections 406/420/201/ 109 of the Penal Code, 1860 on 9-5-2016. 

 20. Let us examine the above mentioned issues in respect of the facts discussed above and in the light of the relevant laws. It appears that the date of occurrence was during the period of April 1998 to May 2001. The allegations were under sections 406/420/201/ 109 of the Penal Code, 1860. At the time of commission of alleged offences the relevant law was "The Anti-Corruption Act, 1957. Sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 were in the schedule of the said Act, 1957. The Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 came into force with effect from 9-5-2004. Though section 38(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 repealed the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957 with effect from 9-5-2004 but section 38(2) and (3) of the said Act saved/protected the proceeding initiated by the Bureau. Section 38(2) keeps provision that unless and until the commission is constituted, the effectiveness of the Anti-Corruption Ad, 1957 would continue as if the said Act has not been repealed. On the other hand, section 38(3) keeps provision that if any inquiry, investigation and approval for lodging case under the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957 are pending those would be completed by the ACC. For better understanding section 38 is reproduced as below— 

 21. In the instant case though inquiry was started by the Bureau but before lodging the FIR, Bureau was abolished. At the same time though ACC Act, 2004 came into force on 9-5-2004 but commission was constituted on 21-11-2004. In this situation as per section 38(2) all the pending issues of the Bureau were required to be dealt with by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption. Therefore, in view of the above provision of section 38(2), inspector of Bureau of Anti-Corruption rightly lodged an FIR on 17-8-2004 for the occurrence allegedly committed in the year 1998 to 2001 under sections 406/420/ 201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860. In view of the above we don't find any illegality in initiation of the instant case by the Bureau against the present petitioner No.1. 

 22. It further appears that subsequent to the lodging of the FIR, the Bureau of Anti-Corruption/The Anti-Corruption Act, 1957 was finally repealed/abolished on 21-11-2004 by constituting the Commission. In view of the above facts if we read sections 20 together with 38(3) of ACC Act, 2004 then it would be very much clear that after repelling the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957, the ACC has absolute jurisdiction to investigate the case filed by the Bureau under the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957, therefore, the decision of the ACC to investigate the Case by the officer of the ACC does not suffer from any legal infirmity. In view of the above, we also don't find any violation of section 20 of the ACC, Act, 2004 or illegality in investigation and submission of charge-sheet against the petitioners by the ACC though sections 406/420/201 were not in the schedule of the ACC Act, 2004. In this regard in the case of ACC vs Sheikh Amin Uddin, reported in 69 DLR (AD) 373; 5 CLR (AD) (2017) 66 our Apex Court also held that the Ain clearly provides that the investigation into any allegation pending under the repealed Act shall be performed by the Commission under the Ain. 

 23. We have also meticulously examined the charge framing order it appears that FIR was lodged on 17-8-2004 under sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 and the charge-sheets were submitted under sections 406/420/201/109 on 28.02.2012 and the learned Judge framed charge under sections 406/420/ 201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 on 9-5-2015. Though section 109 was not in the schedule of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957 but we don't find any illegality in the charge framing order on the grounds-firstly, the said sections 406/420/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 were in the schedule of the Anti-Corruption Act,1957 and the petitioners are being tried with offences committed under the schedule of the Anti-Corruption Act,1957 pursuant to the FIR dated 17-8-2004; and secondly, though section 109 of the Penal Code, 1860 was not in the schedule of the Anti- Corruption Act, 1957 but as per section 5(7) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act,1958, Special Judge may also charge with and try other offences not so triable with which the accused may, under the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1898, relating to the joinder or charges, be charged at the same trial. In view of the above we hold that the learned Judge rightly framed charge under sections 109 of the Penal Code, 1860 with other schedule offences. The petitioner's submissions so far section 222 of the Code, we are of the view that in view of the provision of 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 a person accused of more offences than one punishable under this Act may be tried at one trial for all such offences.  30. In view of the discussion made above we are of the view that there is no illegality in lodging the FIR by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption, submission of charge-sheet by the ACC as well as in the order framing of charge under sections 406/420/201/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 by Special Judge.
